question_answered: Can an authorized owner obtain an exact working duplicate of a T5502/HCS301 credential with (a) no physical enclosure access, (b) no administrative access, or (c) no receiver participation at all, and how should seller 'clone/copy/autocopy' claims be assessed?
applicability_to_t5502_hcs301: Direct at the architecture level if the unit is a genuine HCS301-based T5502: HCS301 uses a secret key and changing synchronization counter, while the receiver learns transmitter state. Direct product evidence identifies T5502 as 433.92 MHz rolling code and says self-learning is available only for some receivers. [uncertain] Exact conclusions about one installation depend on receiver model, firmware, code mode, and whether the observed T5502 is a genuine/revision-matched unit.
authorization_assumption: Assessment is limited to a verified owner or explicitly authorized administrator seeking continuity of access. It does not authorize bypassing the receiver's administrator, shared-property controls, or credential policy.
key_findings: No physical enclosure access: a new distinct credential may be feasible when a compatible receiver explicitly supports remote-assisted self-learning and the owner has an already enrolled transmitter. This is enrollment, not exact cloning, and the receiver still participates over the air.

No administrative access: lack of a cabinet key is not necessarily lack of delegated authority; a documented mother-transmitter workflow may be an authorized administrative mechanism. If the owner has neither administrator approval nor a receiver-supported delegated workflow, legitimate enrollment is not feasible.

No receiver participation at all: a transmitter can be purchased or factory-provisioned, but it cannot become an accepted new credential through enrollment because the receiver must learn/store transmitter-specific state. Exact duplication from ordinary RF observations is not established by the cited sources.

Microchip documents that HCS301 EEPROM key/configuration data is read-protected and that normal/secure learning derives and stores keys/state at the receiver. Capturing normal transmissions therefore is not equivalent to obtaining an independently maintainable credential.

Seller words such as 'copy,' 'clone,' 'autocopy,' 'learning,' and 'compatible' are not standardized. A valid claim must state whether the product creates a unique credential and enrolls it, relies on the receiver's remote-learn feature, or purports to share the original identity/state.
A seller claim that requires the live receiver to hear a sequence from an existing and new remote is best classified as transmitter-assisted enrollment, even if marketed as copying.

Dealer statement; not proof for an unidentified receiver.

Generic learning-remote document mirrored by Scribd, explicitly says HCS301 and other rolling-code remotes cannot be copied by its fixed-code workflow, https://www.scribd.com/document/1060460140/Learning-Remote-Setup-Document (accessed 2026-10-01). Low-to-moderate quality and product-specific; useful only as counterevidence to broad generic-copy advertising.
evidence_quality: High for HCS301 security architecture, protected memory, and receiver learning semantics due to Microchip primary documentation. High-to-moderate for Hiland R510X and T5502 self-learning behavior due to manufacturer documentation, but the phrase 'some receivers' prevents generalization. Moderate for exact T5502 IC identity and dealer no-enclosure claim. Low for generic marketplace 'clone/autocopy' language unless the vendor supplies a model-specific manual, credential semantics, supported-receiver matrix, and reproducible authorized acceptance test.
source_dates: Microchip HCS301 and HCS515 documents are 2011 revisions/copyright editions; TB003 page is dated 2015-06-24. Hiland manufacturer pages/manual and current dealer pages were retrieved 2026-10-01. The exact date and revision coverage of the T5502 web page are not shown. [uncertain]
source_claim_type: Read protection, code-hopping structure and learning semantics: primary semiconductor manufacturer documentation.
Self-learning and R510X receiver behavior: primary equipment-manufacturer documentation.
No-enclosure programming and broad T5502 compatibility: dealer statement requiring target-receiver verification.
Generic copy exclusions: third-party product instruction with limited provenance.
Three-case feasibility conclusion and classification of seller terminology: evidence-based inference.
relevant_components: T5502/HCS301 transmitter, its battery and RF stage, target receiver/radio module, receiver firmware and credential memory, any enrolled 'mother' transmitter, and the controller's authorized learning interface. Seller devices must be evaluated as complete credential products, not merely by carrier frequency or an advertised chip list.
hardware_revision_and_markings: Required evidence includes T5502 shell and PCB model/revision, HCS301 package marking, RF resonator marking, button count, battery holder, receiver/controller label, receiver radio-module revision, and firmware where available. A shell photo or 'HCS301 compatible' advertisement is insufficient. [uncertain]
power_variant: Public listings conflict between a 12 V 23A/23AE alkaline battery and 3 V CR2032. This likely reflects revisions, listing errors, or variants, but the cause is not established. Verify the physical holder and PCB marking before selecting a replacement; the discrepancy is also a useful authenticity check. [uncertain]
rf_profile: Best-supported characteristics are 433.92 MHz, three channels and rolling code. [uncertain] Exact modulation, timing, bandwidth, and regional variant are not established. Receive-only comparison may confirm carrier and gross waveform compatibility, but it cannot validate the secret provisioning domain or authorize a credential.
observable_data: Lawful non-invasive observations include model/revision labels, battery, button/channel behavior, carrier frequency, transmission length/timing, and receiver response during an authorized enrollment test. Repeated rolling transmissions can demonstrate that frames change, but cannot by themselves prove that a marketed copier creates a durable independently synchronized credential.
protected_or_secret_data: Secret cryptographic key material, OEM/manufacturer-code domain, learn seed, and synchronization state are protected/security-sensitive. HCS301 documentation says EEPROM data holding the crypt key, serial and configuration is not externally readable and is read-protected. No recovery, extraction, fault, cryptanalysis, or derivation procedure is provided.
manufacturer_key_domain_evidence: Acceptable non-secret evidence includes a Hiland/OEM supported-model matrix, written vendor confirmation naming the receiver and transmitter revisions, proof both products belong to the same provisioning family, official receiver-manual support, or a controlled returnable enrollment test. Same frequency, same enclosure, or same HCS301 chip is not enough.
compatibility_constraints: A working result depends on frequency, modulation and timing, transmitter programming, manufacturer-key domain, receiver learning algorithm/policy, receiver firmware, memory availability, button/channel mapping, and regional/legal conformity. Self-learning also depends on an enrolled transmitter and the feature being enabled on that receiver.
variant_conflicts: Conflicts include battery voltage claims, reseller versus manufacturer compatibility language, and ambiguous terms such as 'universal,' 'copy,' and 'self-learning.' Resolve through exact board/receiver identification, official written compatibility, and a supervised returnable test. [uncertain] Do not treat a successful first operation as proof of stable compatibility; the receiver must accept later sequential uses as well.
access_assumption: Case A—no physical enclosure access: RF reach and receiver participation may still exist. Case B—no administrative access: distinguish missing cabinet/login access from lack of authority; an official enrolled-transmitter workflow may itself be delegated administration. Case C—no receiver participation: the receiver neither enters learning nor changes memory, whether locally, remotely, or through an administrator. Also distinguish no RF reach, which prevents over-the-air learning even if authorized.
receiver_dependency: All legitimate add-credential routes depend on the target receiver accepting and storing the new credential, either during local learn mode or remotely triggered learning. Procurement and factory provisioning can occur offline but do not by themselves alter the target receiver. An actual exact clone claim attempts to avoid new enrollment and therefore demands much stronger proof and security scrutiny.
receiver_make_model_firmware: Unknown for the target installation. [uncertain] Establish through exterior labels, owner/installer records, invoice, OEM support, or authorized inspection. Hiland R510X evidence cannot be generalized to every receiver paired with a T5502 or to a private-label controller.
physical_access_vs_receiver_participatio: Physical enclosure access is not always necessary: Hiland documents self-learning for some receivers using an already learned transmitter. Nevertheless, the receiver must be powered, within RF range, enter its learning process, validate transmissions, and store the new credential. Thus 'no receiver access' can be true physically while false functionally.
existing_authorized_remote_required: Yes for the documented transmitter-assisted/no-enclosure route; not necessarily for authorized local learn-button enrollment or receiver replacement. It does not make receiver-free exact cloning proven.
enrollment_method_and_authority: Use only the receiver's official owner/installer workflow. A local learn control is invoked by the authorized administrator; a documented mother-transmitter workflow may delegate learn initiation to a current credential holder. If neither authority path exists, the proper route is OEM/installer service or receiver migration, not an advertised bypass.
credential_semantics: Classify outcomes as: (1) unique credential enrolled into the existing receiver; (2) OEM-domain compatible transmitter awaiting enrollment; (3) receiver migration and fresh credentials; or (4) purported exact clone sharing old identity/state. Marketing terms do not decide the class. Claims in classes 1–3 are plausible with documentation; class 4 is unsubstantiated here and carries synchronization and revocation risks.
receiver_memory_and_revocation: A receiver-enrolled new credential generally consumes or replaces a slot and can often be revoked under receiver-specific rules. A purported exact clone may be indistinguishable from the original to the receiver, frustrating individual revocation and risking counter interaction. Hiland R510X lists model-dependent capacities and erase-all; Microchip HCS515 illustrates overwrite and erase-all semantics. Verify the actual receiver before any test.
legitimate_routes: No enclosure access: documented transmitter-assisted enrollment with owner authorization, a compatible new transmitter, an enrolled mother transmitter, RF reach, and a receiver that explicitly supports the feature.
Authorized administrator or installer enrollment through the receiver's documented interface.
OEM/dealer-supplied compatible transmitter followed by authorized receiver enrollment.
Authorized receiver/radio-module migration with new credentials when legacy compatibility or administration cannot be restored.
Non-invasive identification and receive-only RF characterization before purchase; this is compatibility work, not cloning.
prerequisites: Proof of ownership or administrator approval; exact receiver/transmitter model and revision; official manual or OEM confirmation; compatible frequency/provisioning family; safe RF reach; a working enrolled remote for self-learning; available memory; and a rollback inventory of existing credentials.
equipment_or_service_needed: A genuine supported transmitter, official instructions, and possibly an authorized gate/access-control installer or locksmith. A receive-only spectrum analyzer or SDR can help identify carrier/timing without transmitting or decoding protected content. Receiver migration requires compatible certified hardware and qualified installation. No extraction or cryptographic bypass tooling is within scope.
expected_outcomes: Case A may yield a distinct new enrolled credential without opening the enclosure. Case B yields a credential only if an approved delegated remote-learning mechanism counts as the authorized administration path; otherwise no legitimate change occurs. Case C yields no newly enrolled credential; only an unpaired candidate device or a plan for later service. A validated replacement should work repeatedly while the original remains functional and independently revocable where supported.
limitations: The receiver is unidentified; Hiland says self-learning exists only for some receivers. Seller terminology is inconsistent and may conceal ordinary enrollment. Public sources do not establish a safe receiver-free exact-clone route. Bench success against a test receiver does not prove compatibility with the installed receiver's firmware/key domain. Availability, policy, and regional radio rules can further limit options.
cost_or_effort_band: Claim verification by documentation and returnable purchase: low to medium. Authorized remote-assisted enrollment: low if supported. Installer diagnosis/enrollment: medium. Receiver migration: medium to high. Independent laboratory validation of a vendor's exact-clone claim would be high effort and still inappropriate on a live access system. [uncertain]
route_classification: No-enclosure mother-remote workflow is enrollment; OEM-compatible supply is vendor provisioning/interoperability; installer learn mode is enrollment; new receiver is migration; fixed-code copying is not applicable to a verified HCS301 rolling-code variant; receiver-free identity duplication is unsupported cryptographic duplication.
product_status_and_authenticity: Microchip lists HCS301 as In Production, but the exact T5502 lifecycle/revision remains unclear. [uncertain] Validate seller identity, genuine-source evidence, PCB photos, supported receiver list, warranty, return policy, and whether 'clone' actually means enroll. Avoid products whose only support is a long chip-name list, frequency match, unverifiable demonstrations, or a request to disclose secret values.
feasibility_without_receiver: No physical enclosure access: conditionally feasible for a new credential if the live receiver supports authorized over-the-air self-learning; confidence moderate pending receiver ID. No administrative access: not legitimately feasible unless an official delegated enrolled-transmitter procedure is itself the authorized administrative mechanism. No receiver participation at all: enrollment is infeasible by definition, and exact receiver-free duplication is not substantiated. Buying a transmitter or observing RF does not change that conclusion.
confidence: High on the distinction between physical access and receiver participation, and high that receiver enrollment stores credential state in documented HCS301 architectures. Moderate on T5502-specific no-enclosure feasibility because Hiland limits self-learning to some receivers. High that bare seller words 'clone/copy/autocopy' are insufficient evidence. The conclusion is deliberately narrower than claiming theoretical impossibility of every laboratory attack; no bypass assessment or method is provided.
legal_or_authorization_notes: Possession of an original remote is not necessarily authority to add credentials, especially for shared gates, rentals, workplaces, or managed parking. Obtain owner/administrator consent and follow local radio, access-control, tenancy, and computer-misuse laws. Seek local legal advice if authority or the legality of third-party credential duplication is disputed.
operational_risks: Risks include unintended gate motion, enrollment of an unintended transmitter while learn mode is open, memory overwrite or erase-all lockout, loss of auditability, counter desynchronization, original-and-clone interference, inability to revoke only one of two shared identities, false confidence after a one-time success, RF interference, and damage from the wrong battery variant.
enrollment_side_effects: A receiver may consume a slot, overwrite a prior slot when full, replace what it considers a duplicate, or require erase-all to revoke lost credentials. Remote learning temporarily changes receiver state. An alleged exact identity clone could couple the two devices' synchronization behavior and revocation fate. Test only with the site secured and all valid credentials inventoried.
prohibited_actionable_details_omitted: Yes. Key/seed extraction, cryptographic attacks, rolling-code defeat, replay, brute force, protected-memory access, and unauthorized-access procedures are omitted.
stop_conditions: Stop if authority is unclear; the receiver cannot be identified; the seller cannot define whether its product enrolls or clones; the product requires secret extraction or interception; learn/erase behavior is undocumented; the gate moves unexpectedly; safety sensors or manual release are unavailable; any existing remote stops working; memory capacity/revocation is unknown; or the device passes only once and then diverges. Escalate to Hiland/OEM, an authorized installer or qualified access-control locksmith, or legal counsel.
recommended_next_steps: Replace the phrase 'without receiver access' with the exact constraint: no enclosure access, no administrator permission/interface, no RF reach, or no receiver participation.
Identify the installed receiver/controller and confirm whether its official manual supports mother-transmitter/self-learning for this T5502 revision.
Ask each vendor to state in writing whether the offered product creates a unique credential and requires the target receiver to be in learning mode.
Prefer a genuine returnable transmitter and a supervised authorized enrollment test over any receiver-free clone claim.
If administration cannot be recovered, have the owner commission receiver/radio-module migration and fresh credentials, then revoke the legacy system.
Record acceptance results and maintain a credential inventory.
questions_for_owner_or_vendor: What exact receiver model, firmware, and code mode is installed?
Does 'copy/clone/autocopy' mean receiver enrollment, transfer of button selection, or shared identity/state?
Must the target receiver be powered and within range during setup, and does its memory change?
Is an already enrolled transmitter required, and is that workflow documented by the receiver manufacturer?
Which exact T5502 PCB/battery revision and receiver models were tested?
Will both old and new transmitters work alternately for many supervised cycles and remain independently revocable?
What happens when receiver memory is full, and what is the rollback procedure?
What authenticity, warranty, return, and regional-certification evidence is provided?
rollback_and_acceptance_test: Before testing, inventory all remotes/channels, preserve the original, record controller settings, verify manual release and safety sensors, and secure the gate area with an observer. Use only a documented enrollment path and one new transmitter. Pass criteria: repeated alternating uses of original and new transmitter on every intended channel; no unexpected relay/channel behavior; all pre-existing credentials still work; safety functions remain normal; and the administrator can identify/revoke the new credential as the manual promises. A single successful activation is insufficient. On failure, stop transmitting, use documented individual deletion if available, and have the installer restore the recorded state; do not perform erase-all unless every valid credential is present for controlled re-enrollment.
